statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk 8% (low). NQZ26 prints 31,056.25 on Yahoo Finance at 05:17Z and 31,056.75 on Investing.com, -0.02% against a 31,061.75 prior close, after a fresh 31,036.75 session low printed and roughly 20 points were recovered. The 31,221.25 high has stood unretested for more than three hours and the full session range is 0.59%. ES -0.11% and YM -0.14% sit near their own session lows, so no aligned one-way complex exists. Stress holds 54% (elevated) as Brent 101.48 and WTI 90.40 tick up off session lows and the 10-year yield is confirmed to have reversed higher to about 5.29% on 2 October. Confidence 87% (high).
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the mapped policy state is EA_ON and the published forecast path holds EA_ON across all 24 hours with a 7% floor and a 12% peak. The narrow danger window spans 13:00-15:00Z on 5 October, 15:00-17:00 Berlin, covering the 13:30Z US cash open, the S&P Global composite and services finals at 13:45Z and September ISM Services at 14:00Z. That window is published on scheduled-catalyst grounds rather than on observed one-way structure. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection are unaffected.
headline: Tail holds 8% as a fresh 31,036.75 low is absorbed inside a 0.59% range, with ES and YM near their own lows and a confirmed 10-year yield reversal to 5.29% keeping Stress flat at 54%
body:
The invalidation level named in the previous assessment has been breached, and scoring that honestly is the main task of this hour. NQZ26 prints 31,056.25 on Yahoo Finance at 05:17:27Z and 31,056.75 on Investing.com at 05:17:46Z, down 5.50 and 5.00 points against a 31,061.75 prior close, a decline of 0.02% on 51.46k contracts. The session low is no longer 31,059.00; a fresh 31,036.75 low printed during this hour, and price has since recovered roughly 20 points from it. The session range is therefore 31,036.75 to 31,221.25, a span of 184.5 points or 0.59%, and the 31,221.25 high has now stood unretested for more than three hours.

The previous hour published an 8% Tail on the thesis that a completed round-trip was holding about 15 points above the then-low. That specific low did not hold. The correct response is neither to ignore the break nor to react mechanically to it. The downside extension measures 22 points, or 0.07%, it was absorbed within the same hour, and price now sits back in the lower third of a range that is itself only 0.59% wide. The contract names shallow or absent pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements, and holding near session extremes as the amplifiers that justify protection. Price is nearer the low than the high, which is a mild version of the third condition, but the first two are plainly absent: the single upside extension failed once and has not been retried for three hours, and the downside extension was immediately bought back rather than extended. Tail therefore holds at 8% rather than decaying to a lower floor, mapping to EA_ON and green with the dominant mode normal. Holding the score rather than lowering it is the whole adjustment: the path has not deteriorated, but the evidence no longer supports further improvement.

The cross-asset picture is directionally aligned but trivial in magnitude, which is the distinction that matters here. ES trades 7,768.75, down 0.11% in a 7,765.75 to 7,793.00 range and about 3 points off its low. YM trades 51,405.00, down 0.14% in a 51,377.00 to 51,560.00 range and about 28 points off its low. All three index futures are mildly negative and near session lows, which is alignment of a kind, but a complex that is down one tenth of one percent is not a one-way path; it is a quiet session drifting. Against that, the Nikkei 225 trades 69,750.48, up 1,441.02 points or 2.11% from a 68,309.46 prior close, having traded as high as 70,072.13 and crossed 70,000 intraday before fading some 322 points off that high. A 2.1% regional advance that the Nasdaq-100 declines to follow, and which is itself fading from its own extreme, is evidence against a developing global one-way impulse rather than for one.

One piece of evidence from the previous hour requires correction. That assessment described yields as retreating on the payrolls print, resting on the H.15 series, which last published 4.78% at two years and 5.24% at ten years for 1 October. The H.15 series lags by a session, and the verified 2 October market wrap records the 10-year moving from roughly 5.17% immediately after the weak jobs data back to 5.2939%, a gain of 5.99 basis points on the day. Yields reversed higher on Friday rather than falling. That matters because a record Nasdaq-100 close of 30,807.93, up 1.00%, alongside a 10-year yield pressing back toward 5.30% is a cross-asset conflict, not the benign falling-yield backdrop previously described. A conflict of that kind belongs in Stress and in Confidence, not in Tail, and it is the reason Stress does not continue its three-hour decline.

The energy complex has stopped falling. Brent trades 101.48, down 0.75% in a 101.18 to 103.39 range, and WTI trades 90.40, down 0.78% in an 89.69 to 91.85 range. Both have ticked up off the session lows they were pressing an hour ago, so the cooling that pulled Stress down across the three previous hours has paused rather than continued. The backdrop remains a genuinely difficult one: Brent above 100, a Strait of Hormuz closure now past Day 218 with flows described by analysts as structurally impaired, and a labour market that produced 29,000 September payrolls against an 84,000 to 90,000 consensus, unemployment at 4.2%, and average hourly earnings up 0.1% to 37.81 dollars. With crude no longer fading, yields confirmed higher, and the index complex drifting to session lows, Stress holds flat at 54% and remains elevated. It does not rise, because none of these is a new deterioration; it does not fall, because the three conditions that justified the earlier decline have each stopped applying.

Confidence eases one point to 87%, which remains high. The evidence set is dense and current: two independent live NQ quotes, live ES, YM and Nikkei prints, live Brent and WTI, the primary BLS employment release, the H.15 yield series, and a verified 2 October market wrap that resolved the yield question left open above. The honest limits are specific. Cash VIX and cash Treasuries are closed, so the 15.31 VIX reading is a 2 October close rather than a live level, and H.15 lags a session. The economic-calendar page returned values in an actuals column for releases that are still days in the future, which cannot be genuine; that column was discarded entirely and the calendar was used only for scheduled timing, with no actual published for any unreleased event. The shared Finviz context file carries a 29 September collection timestamp, roughly 7,580 minutes old, with a partial collection status and recorded calendar and futures adapter failures, so it was treated as unusable and this assessment rests entirely on independent research. The small easing in Confidence reflects the structural ambiguity introduced by the breached invalidation level rather than any thinning of the price evidence itself.

The published path holds EA_ON across all 24 hours. It stays at 8% through the final Tokyo hour, eases to a 7% floor as the Asian session is assumed to mature, allows 9% for the 07:00Z European cash-open liquidity transition, returns to the floor through the European morning, and rises to 11% and a 12% session peak across the 13:00Z and 14:00Z hours carrying the US cash open, the S&P Global composite and services finals and September ISM Services. Those increases are scheduled-catalyst allowances, not claims about structure that cannot yet be observed. The path then decays through the US afternoon, allows 10% for the power hour into the 20:00Z cash close, drops to the floor across the assumed 21:00Z maintenance halt, and holds 8% through the overnight handoff into 6 October.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published hours are available from Claude history, and every one mapped to EA_ON and green with the dominant mode normal. Tail was held at 3% from 05:00Z through 21:00Z on 4 October because the CME equity-index complex was halted for the weekend and no Nasdaq-100 price path was scoreable. It then rose through the Sunday reopen as the overnight drift extended and an early shallow pullback was absorbed: 12% in the 22:00Z slot, 13% at 23:00Z, 14% at 00:00Z and a 15% peak at 01:00Z on 5 October. It eased to 13% at 02:00Z once the fresh 31,221.25 high failed, to 10% at 03:00Z once the retracement completed through the prior close, and to 8% at 04:00Z as that round-trip appeared to hold. Stress ran a 79% ceiling at 09:00Z on 4 October on accumulating weekend Hormuz and Gulf incident flow, eased through the 73%, 70%, 68% and 66% readings into a 64% trough at 14:00Z as those headlines failed to transmit into crude, drifted back to 71% by 21:00Z, and then settled through 66%, 65%, 64%, 62%, 60%, 57% and 54% across the seven reopen hours. Confidence held a narrow 83% to 88% band, densest in the European and early US hours and thinnest across the weekend halt and the earliest reopen hours.
